market_summary: US equities bounced on election day (Nasdaq +0.83%, S&P +0.36%) as AI names rallied, while Dow lagged (-0.38%) on rotation. SGX banks sold off hard after UOB's Q3 profit miss (-5.4%) raised concern about margin compression ahead of DBS (Nov 5) and OCBC (Nov 6) results, dragging the whole local banking complex below its 50-day average. In the US, the Democratic midterm sweep in Texas/Georgia on data-center moratoriums is a fresh regulatory overhang for AI infrastructure buildouts and for Musk-linked ventures (Tesla, SpaceX) with major Texas operations, even as Nvidia regained the title of world's most valuable company on continued AI chip demand. Alphabet remains the biggest loser among mega-caps, down ~19% in a month and freshly downgraded by Citizens.

picks.thesis: UOB just missed consensus Q3 net profit by ~9% on weaker trading income and margin pressure, triggering a 5.4% single-day drop to a 4-month low. Momentum is firmly negative (-12% 1m, -12% 3m), relative volume is 3.3x normal confirming distribution, and analyst sentiment is lukewarm (mostly Hold). This looks like the start of a de-rating rather than a one-day overreaction, especially with NIM pressure likely to persist into Q4 guidance.
picks.news: UOB Q3 net profit of S$1.25B missed the ~S$1.37B consensus; shares fell 5.4% to a 4-month low on Nov 3, 2026.
picks.risks: If management commentary on the earnings call signals NIM stabilization or a buyback/dividend surprise, the stock could snap back quickly given it is now cheap vs. its 52-week range (+14% from 52w low).

picks.thesis: Musk spent a record $474M on the midterms (including $224M in Texas alone) and the Democratic sweep there is being read as a rejection of his political strategy, creating potential new regulatory friction for Tesla and SpaceX operations concentrated in Texas. The stock has already run up 24% over 3 months and 5% over the past month, leaving it vulnerable to a sentiment reversal; it fell 1.3% today even as the broader market rallied, suggesting the news is starting to bite.
picks.news: CNBC (Nov 4, 2026) reports Musk's election gamble backfired with a Democratic sweep in Texas, creating political risk for Tesla/SpaceX's Texas operations.
picks.risks: Tesla's business is not directly regulated by state data-center policy, so the read-through could prove more political narrative than fundamental; a strong delivery or margin print could override the headline risk.

picks.thesis: Alphabet is down 19% in a month and nearly 23% over 3 months, the worst momentum in the mega-cap group, now 30% off its 52-week high and underperforming even the Nasdaq-100 decline. Citizens cut it to Market Perform on Oct 29 after a ~14% slide since, and the trend remains broken (16.8% below its 50-day average). This is a clear relative-weakness short versus peers like Nvidia/Microsoft that are participating in the AI rally.
picks.news: Citizens downgraded Alphabet from Outperform to Market Perform on Oct 29, 2026, with the stock down ~13.8% since; shares remain deeply below both 50- and 200-day moving averages.
picks.risks: At 43% implied upside to consensus target and heavily oversold, a short-covering bounce or reassurance on cloud/AI capex returns could reverse the trend quickly.

picks.thesis: Nvidia reclaimed the title of world's most valuable company on Nov 4 as AI demand remains the dominant driver of market cap leadership, even though the stock is still 13.6% off its 52-week high and down 13.5% over the past month, giving a reasonable entry point relative to the move. Analyst coverage is overwhelmingly bullish (59 buys vs 2 holds) with consensus target implying 58% upside, and earnings on Nov 17 are a near-term catalyst.
picks.news: 247wallst.com (Nov 4, 2026): Nvidia's market cap rose 2% to $4.99T, overtaking Apple, on continued AI chip demand.
picks.risks: The Democratic sweep's data-center moratorium push in Texas/Georgia could slow hyperscaler capex, which is Nvidia's core demand driver; a disappointing Nov 17 earnings print given elevated volatility (37% annualized) would hurt.

picks.thesis: Singtel just expanded its partnership with NUHS and Ericsson to build the world's first 6G AI healthcare centre, a positive strategic signal ahead of its Nov 13 earnings. The stock has the most bullish analyst skew on the watchlist (13 buys, 0 sells) with 26% implied upside to target, and it was one of the few gainers today (+1.5%) while banks sold off.
picks.news: Singtel, NUHS and Ericsson signed an MOU on Nov 3-4, 2026 to build the world's first 6G AI healthcare centre.
picks.risks: The deal is strategic/long-term and unlikely to move near-term earnings; stock remains in a longer downtrend (-10% over 6 months, below its 200-day average), so a weak Nov 13 earnings print could override the positive headline.
